I am a 32-year-old woman farmer in Quzhou County. Though I never went to school, I have been working these fields since I was a small child helping my parents, so I know every mu of my 4.1 mu farm. It is just my household of two now—my husband works off-farm at a factory in town, so I manage most of the cropping myself. With only 4.1 mu, I cannot afford to waste land or time, and because my husband is away, I choose labor-saving methods wherever they do not hurt the yield.

For wheat, I plant the full 4.1 mu in October after the maize comes off. I use our own saved improved wheat seeds—about 30–35 jin per mu—because they have performed reliably for years and I do not have to buy them. I rotary-till the field before sowing to prepare a good seedbed. For fertilizer, I broadcast compound fertilizer at basal and topdress with urea in spring; altogether I apply about 18 kg of nitrogen, 10 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I irrigate three times from our well: once in winter, and twice more at green-up and grain-filling. I spray three times for weeds and insects. I expect around 950 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, time is tight after wheat harvest in June, so I plant immediately using no-tillage direct seeding into the wheat stubble. I always buy hybrid maize seed from the agricultural shop—saved maize seed loses too much yield. I apply compound fertilizer at planting, about 15 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice during the summer, at the big trumpet and filling stages. I spray three times to control weeds and corn borers. I expect about 1,100 kg per mu.
